title: Prohibition Against Private Slaughter Offerings
description: The Lord gives through Moses a strict command to Aaron, his sons, and all the Israelites that all slaughter of cattle, sheep, and goats must take place at the entrance to the tent of meeting, where the priest sprinkles the blood on the altar and burns the fat as an offering to the Lord. The purpose is that the people should no longer offer sacrifices to the hairy demons in the open fields. Anyone – including foreigners living among them – who slaughters or offers a sacrifice outside the tent of meeting shall be considered guilty of bloodguilt and must be cut off from the people.
